newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco mayor to unveil stadium guarantee.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco mayor to unveil stadium guarantee.

text.p: San Francisco Mayor Willie Brown plans to unveil an agreement on Tuesday that would guarantee the city never would have to dip into its general fund to pay off bonds for a proposed stadium-mall complex, a spokesman for the mayor said.

Spokesman P.J. Johnston said the mayor and city finance officials were finalizing the proposal, which would guarantee that the city's general fund would remain untouched if tax revenues generated by the project fell below projections.
"It would absolutely remove any doubt about the city's general fund exposure," Johnston said of the plan.

San Francisco residents on June 3 will vote on a $100 million lease revenue bond measure that would help to finance the city's share of the proposed $525 million San Francisco 49ers football stadium and shopping complex.
Brown will announce his plan to protect the city's general fund at a press conference Tuesday, his office said.
The San Francisco Chronicle newspaper reported that the guarantee would be provided by Morgan Stanley Group Inc, which would take a lead role in securing the project's private financing.
